correctness.rationale: The two-step Laplacian identity forces complementary firing phases, and the exact positive-width vertex intervals are both necessary and sufficient. Their four biclique vertex classes give equation (1) without omitting degenerate shores. Direct labelled orbit counting gives the balanced trace representation; polynomial moments diagonalize the binomial transition matrix, yielding exact falling-factorial eigenvalues. Uniform two-binomial local CLT plus explicit endpoint upper bound proves the arcsine weak limit; Gaussian Riemann domination proves the square-root count asymptotic. The extracted standalone exact-arithmetic verifier independently agrees on 51,556 confined labelled small states and symbolic identities, but finite tests alone do not prove infinite limits.

value.rationale: Conserved chip mass makes the full orbit-mass polynomial a natural physical invariant. The exact polynomial and spectral falling-factorial sum solve an all-parameter quantitative census for an infinite graph family, not merely period existence. A uniform periodic-orbit phase has a nonconcentrating Beta(1/2,1/2) firing fraction, structurally distinct from complete-graph Gaussian phase balance; this identifies an unusual macroscopic split in coupled bipartite sandpiles. The finite formulas and asymptotic distribution provide motivated comparisons for recurrent-state ensemble studies. The claim neither requires nor asserts attraction-basin classification.
